figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1.
(A) Outline of the Taxol biosynthetic pathway. The cyclization of geranylgeranyl diphosphate to taxadiene by taxadiene synthase and the hydroxylation
to taxadien-5a-ol by taxadiene 5a-hydroxylase (a), the acetylation of taxadien-5a-ol by taxa-4(20),11(12)-dien-5a-ol-O-acetyl transferase (b), the conversion of
10-deacetylbaccatin III (10-DAB) to baccatin III by 10-deacetylbaccatin III-10-O-acetyl transferase (DBAT) (c), and the side-chain attachment to baccatin III to form
Taxol (d) are highlighted. The broken arrow indicates several as yet undeﬁned steps. (B) Postulated biosynthetic scheme for the formation of the oxetane, present
in Taxol and related late-stage taxoids, in which the 4(20)-ene-5a-ol is converted to the 4(20)-ene-5a-yl acetate, followed by epoxidation to the 4(20)-epoxy-
5a-acetoxy group and then intramolecular rearrangement to the 4-acetoxy oxetane moiety. Ac, acetyl; Bz, benzoyl; t-BOC, tertiary-butoxycarbonyl; OPP,
diphosphate.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2.
Radio-HPLC analysis of the biosynthetic product (retention time 5
7.0 6 0.1 min) generated from 10-DAB and [2-3H]acetyl CoA by the recombi-
nant acetyl transferase. The UV proﬁle (Upper) and the coincident radioac-
tivity proﬁle (Lower) coincide with the retention time of authentic baccatin III.
For column, solvent, ﬂow rates, and counting details, see Materials and
Methods.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3.
Combined reverse-phase HPLC-atmospheric pressure chemical ion-
ization MS analysis of the biosynthetic product (retention time 5 8.6 6 0.1
min) generated by the recombinant acetyl transferase with 10-DAB and acetyl
CoA as cosubstrates (Upper spectrum) and of authentic baccatin III (retention
time 5 8.6 6 0.1 min; Lower spectrum). The diagnostic mass spectral fragment
ions are at myz 605 (P 1 NH41), 587 (PH1), 572 (PH1 2 CH3), 527 (PH1 2
CH3COOH), and 509 (PH1 2 (CH3COOH 2 H2O). For column, solvent, ﬂow rates,
and instrument details, see Materials and Methods.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4.
Deduced amino acid sequence comparison of DBAT (accession no. AF193765) from T. cuspidata, taxadien-5a-ol-O-acetyl transferase (TAT, accession no.
AF190130) from T. cuspidata, benzylalcohol acetyl transferase (BEAT, accession no. AF043464) from Clarkia breweri, and deacetylvindoline-4-O-acetyl transferase
(DAT, accession no. AF053307) from Catharanthus roseus. Residues boxed in black indicate positional identity for at least two of the compared sequences; similar
amino acids are indicated by gray shading. Asterisks (*) indicate conserved residues in all acetyl transferase sequences of plant origin. Pound signs (#) indicate
a putative acyl group transfer motif (HXXXDG) present in three of the four sequences. The alignment was created with the PILEUP program (Wisconsin Package
Version 9.0; Genetics Computer Group, Madison, WI).
